memory_verse: "He who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will give life to your mortal bodies through His Spirit." —Romans 8:11, NASB
sermon_title: A Freedom Only Christ Can Give

days.message_reflection: The sermon described a hypothetical 'external life certificate' that has a disclaimer — it does not certify the inner life that only God sees. Thinking honestly about your own life this past week, what would the disclaimer on your certificate say?
days.verse_reflection: Romans 8:11 says the Spirit who raised Christ from the dead dwells in you and will give life to your mortal body. Romans 8:9 says that if the Spirit of God truly dwells in you, you are not in the flesh but in the Spirit. On an ordinary Monday — in your private thoughts, your reactions at home, your attitudes when no one is watching — is the life of the indwelling Spirit actually visible, or are you living as though He is not there?

days.focus: God Sees the Heart, Not the Outward Appearance
days.message_reflection: The sermon pointed out that on the day we stand before the Lord, God will not be looking at what others thought of us but at what was on the inside — our thoughts, motives, and attitudes. What is one specific area of your inner life this week that you have been more concerned about managing before people than bringing honestly before God?
days.verse_reflection: Romans 8:5-8 draws a sharp line: the mind set on the flesh is death, but the mind set on the Spirit is life and peace. The Spirit who gives life to your mortal body in Romans 8:11 is the same Spirit whose leading determines whether your mind is set on flesh or on God. When you examine the actual direction of your thoughts and desires today — not your outward conduct, but the inside of the cup — which way is your mind genuinely set, and are you willing to be specific with God about what you find?

days.focus: The Freedom Jesus Came to Proclaim
days.message_reflection: The sermon noted that Jesus deliberately searched out Luke 4:18 as the text for His very first sermon, and that Paul's first recorded sermon carried the same burden in Acts 13:39 — freedom from what the law of Moses could never free us from. According to what was preached, what is the specific bondage that both Jesus and Paul were addressing in people who already had a good external, religious testimony?
days.verse_reflection: Romans 8:2 says the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set you free from the law of sin and death — and Romans 8:11 grounds that freedom in the same Spirit who raised Christ living in you now. Acts 13:39 says you are freed from all things the law of Moses could not free you from. Have you actually experienced this as a present reality in your daily life, or do you still treat freedom from the power of sin as something theoretical — something you hope for rather than something the indwelling Spirit is meant to produce in you today?

days.focus: Recognizing Your Need: The Sick Who Come to the Physician
days.message_reflection: The sermon contrasted two kinds of people in the room: those who are focused on maintaining a good external testimony before others, and those who are willing to say to God, 'Everything is not okay — I want to turn over the cup and show you what is inside.' Which of those two descriptions more honestly fits where you have been living this week, and what would it look like practically for you to stop pretending?
days.verse_reflection: Paul's cry in Romans 7:24 — 'Who will set me free from the body of this death?' — leads directly into the answer of Romans 8:1-2 and the life-giving Spirit of Romans 8:11. The physician in Luke 5:31 comes for those who acknowledge they are sick, not for those who are managing appearances. Are you coming to God this week as someone who genuinely knows they are sick and needs the Spirit's life, or are you treating your daily quiet time as one more external religious activity that keeps the outside of the cup looking acceptable?

days.focus: Do You Wish to Be Well? — The Question Jesus Asks
days.message_reflection: The sermon drew attention to the fact that Jesus did not ask the man at Bethesda whether he could make himself well — He asked whether he wished to be well. The sermon also mentioned people who have tried for years to be free from sins like anxiety, lust, anger, and unforgiveness and have quietly settled into living with that condition. Is there any area of inner bondage where you have stopped genuinely wishing to be well and have simply learned to manage it or hide it?
days.verse_reflection: Galatians 5:16 says walk by the Spirit and you will not carry out the desire of the flesh — not 'try harder by your own effort,' but walk by the Spirit. Romans 8:11 promises that the same Spirit who raised Jesus from the dead is available to give life to your mortal body — your very desires, impulses, and habitual reactions. Are there specific fleshly desires listed in Galatians 5:19-21 that you have been fighting in your own strength for so long that you have quietly given up, when what God is actually offering is the life-giving power of His own Spirit dwelling in you?

days.focus: Living for God's Opinion, Not Man's — A Week's Honest Review
days.message_reflection: The sermon said there are going to be two types of people who walk out of that service: those who care about what others think of their external testimony, and those who say, 'Lord, what do you think of my life? You see me 24/7.' As you look back over Monday through Saturday this week, which of those two orientations has actually been driving your choices and attitudes in the moments when no one else was watching?
days.verse_reflection: Romans 8:12-14 says we are debtors — not to the flesh to live according to it — but that if by the Spirit we put to death the deeds of the body, we will live, and those who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God. Romans 8:11 is not simply a comforting promise about physical resurrection; it is about the Spirit making a practical, present difference in your mortal body now. As this week closes, can you point to even one specific moment where you were actually led by the Spirit — where a sinful thought, attitude, or reaction was put to death not by your own willpower but by consciously depending on the life of the Spirit within you?
